newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to export 53,000 T sugar to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to export 53,000 T sugar to U.S.

text.p: The United States will import 53,000 tonnes of Philippine sugar in January, 1997, Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) chief Wilson Gamboa said on Wednesday.
The Philippines has so far exported 78,000 tonnes of sugar since the start of its 1996-1997 crop year ending August.

The Philippines is a beneficiary of a programme under which developing nations export sugar to the United States at premium prices. It has an allocation of 219,000 tonnes of sugar to the United States in the current crop year.
Gamboa said the export of this consignment of 53,000 tonnes would help reduce the country's sugar glut.
In October, the government banned sugar imports until March 1997 to protect local farmers.
Despite abundant local supplies of sugar, traders have been wanting to import because it is cheaper.
President Fidel Ramos has formed a Cabinet-level task force to address the oversupply situation and help farmers hurt by the situation, Gamboa said.
Farmers said the farm-gate price of sugar had dropped to 525 pesos per 50-kilo bag from 800 pesos last year.
